note: Language data for caption.py. Regexes are Python syntax, flags inline.

messages.first_line_blank: the caption opens on a blank line
messages.first_line_tag: opens on a hashtag or a mention, which is the one position worth a sentence
messages.first_line_cut: {chars} characters, so it gets cut at {cut} mid-thought. Fine if the cut is a cliffhanger, bad if it is a subordinate clause
messages.hook_concrete: {count} number(s) or name(s) in the visible window
messages.hook_abstract: {count} number(s) or name(s) in the visible window - nothing checkable before the tap
messages.hashtags_over: {count} tags, over Instagram's cap of {limit}. Tags past the fifth do not count and the block reads as old
messages.hashtags_cap_generic: {count} tags, at the cap, and {generic} of them generic. Spend the five on topics
messages.hashtags_generic: {count} tags, {generic} of them generic ({examples}). Those describe nothing
messages.placement_window: a hashtag is inside the visible window, spending feed space on a label
messages.links_found: {count} link(s) in the caption, and captions are not clickable. Move it to the bio or the DM
messages.links_none: no dead links in the body
messages.ask_none: no call to action. Decide what this post is for
messages.ask_many: {count} asks ({asks}). Two asks is the same as none
messages.emoji_decoration: {count} emoji, {density:.1f} per 100 characters - reads as decoration
messages.head: CAPTION LINT  ·  {chars} / {limit} chars  ·  {tags} hashtags  ·  {asks} ask(s)

auto.note: Function words --lang auto counts to guess the language of a text. Same list in every en file.
